title: A Hot Mic Helped Convict Robert Durst

narration: Robert Durst volunteered for a television interview.
Then he went to the bathroom wearing a live mic.

sources.claim_text: Robert Durst was a New York real-estate heir ('scion' of the Durst family). Narration: 'Robert Durst'; label: 'NEW YORK REAL-ESTATE HEIR'.

Durst approached the filmmaker after the 2010 feature 'All Good Things' and volunteered to be interviewed for the HBO series 'The Jinx' (THR: about 21 hours of interviews, not stated). Narration: 'Robert Durst volunteered for a television interview.'

After the final interview (recorded 18 April 2012) he went to the bathroom still wearing a live microphone and was recorded saying, among other remarks, 'There it is. You're caught.' and 'What the hell did I do? Killed them all, of course.' The finale aired on 15 March 2015. Narration: 'Then he went to the bathroom wearing a live mic.' / 'It caught him: killed them all, of course.' The card says 'wording as reported'.

narration: His wife vanished in 1982. His best friend was shot dead in 2000.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit -> sit_slumped; detective: read -> stand -> arms_crossed; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'TWO WOMEN · 18 YEARS APART', card '1982 · HIS WIFE VANISHED · NEVER FOUND / 2000 · HIS BEST FRIEND SHOT DEAD / AS POLICE PREPARED TO QUESTION HER ABOUT HIS WIFE'.

sources.claim_text: Kathleen McCormack Durst, his first wife, 29 and a medical student, was last seen on 31 January 1982 (Durst said he put her on a train at South Salem, New York); she was never found. Narration: 'His wife vanished in 1982.' Card: '1982 · HIS WIFE VANISHED · NEVER FOUND'. She is named only on the memorial card.

Susan Berman, 55, a writer and his close friend (CBS: 'best friend'), was shot dead at her home near Beverly Hills in December 2000, as New York investigators prepared to question her about Kathleen's disappearance. Narration: 'His best friend was shot dead in 2000.' She is named only on the memorial card; nothing of the crime is shown.

narration: Police got an anonymous note: cadaver, and her address.
shots.visual_description: office day (cold grade); detective: read -> point -> arms_crossed -> point; analyst: stand -> examine -> point; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'BEVERLY HILLS POLICE · DECEMBER 2000', card 'ONE WORD: "CADAVER" / AND HER ADDRESS / THE ENVELOPE SPELT IT "BEVERLEY"'.

sources.claim_text: An anonymous note mailed to Beverly Hills police gave only Berman's address and the word 'CADAVER', in block letters; the envelope misspelled Beverly as 'Beverley'. Narration: 'Police got an anonymous note: cadaver, and her address.' The drawn envelope and note are generic (tag 'NOT THE REAL NOTE'); no address is drawn.

sources.claim_text: Durst denied writing the note for years, to police and to the documentary filmmakers; at trial in August 2021 he admitted writing it but denied the killing. Narration: 'He denied writing it, even to the HBO crew filming him.'

Durst approached the filmmaker after the 2010 feature 'All Good Things' and volunteered to be interviewed for the HBO series 'The Jinx' (THR: about 21 hours of interviews, not stated). Narration: 'Robert Durst volunteered for a television interview.'

narration: The filmmakers found a letter he'd sent her.

sources.claim_text: The Jinx filmmakers found an earlier letter Durst had sent Berman with nearly identical handwriting and the same 'Beverley' misspelling; confronted with the two side by side he could not tell them apart. A law-enforcement official told AP the handwriting analysis linking the letters was the key new evidence given to prosecutors before his arrest; the prosecutor called the note the 'smoking gun'. Narration: 'The filmmakers found a letter he'd sent her.' / 'Same handwriting, same spelling mistake.'

sources.claim_text: After the final interview (recorded 18 April 2012) he went to the bathroom still wearing a live microphone and was recorded saying, among other remarks, 'There it is. You're caught.' and 'What the hell did I do? Killed them all, of course.' The finale aired on 15 March 2015. Narration: 'Then he went to the bathroom wearing a live mic.' / 'It caught him: killed them all, of course.' The card says 'wording as reported'.

CARD ONLY: a 2019 New York Times report on the unedited transcript showed the bathroom remarks were pulled from a longer sequence of rambling remarks and re-ordered; the filmmakers said they put 'killed them all' last for dramatic effect; the editing came out at trial. Card: 'THE AUDIO WAS LATER SHOWN TO BE RE-ORDERED IN EDITING'.

Narration: 'The filmmakers found a letter he'd sent her.' / 'Same handwriting, same spelling mistake.'

sources.claim_text: FBI agents arrested Durst at a New Orleans hotel on Saturday 14 March 2015, the day before the finale aired, on a Los Angeles warrant for Berman's murder. Narration: 'He was arrested the day before it aired.' Card: 'NEW ORLEANS · 14 MARCH 2015'.

sources.claim_text: A Los Angeles jury convicted Durst of the first-degree murder of Susan Berman, with special circumstances, on 17 September 2021. Narration: 'In 2021 a jury convicted him of his friend's murder.'
Judge Mark Windham sentenced him to life without the possibility of parole on 14 October 2021. Narration: 'Sentence: life without parole.'

CARD ONLY: the bathroom recording was played to the jury in Los Angeles during opening statements in March 2020; the trial was paused by the pandemic and resumed in May 2021 with the same jury. Card: 'THE LETTER AND THE TAPE WERE BOTH IN EVIDENCE'.

narration: He died in custody in 2022, charged with his wife's murder too.

sources.claim_text: Durst died of natural causes in custody (at an outside hospital, per the California corrections department) on 10 January 2022, aged 78, while awaiting trial on the Kathleen charge; that case never went to trial. Narration: 'He died in custody in 2022'. Card: 'THAT CASE NEVER WENT TO TRIAL'.

A second-degree murder complaint over Kathleen's death was filed in Lewisboro Town Court on 19 October 2021 and a Westchester County grand jury indictment was reported on 1 November 2021. Narration: 'charged with his wife's murder too'. Card: 'OCT-NOV 2021'.
CARD ONLY (memorial): Kathleen McCormack Durst (29 when last seen in 1982) and Susan Berman (55, killed in 2000). Narration: 'We remember them both.'
